title: Which Drivers' Hours Rules Apply?
whatItIs: Three sets of drivers' hours rules: assimilated (most lorries over 3.5 t, in the UK and UK–EU), AETR (other international journeys) and GB domestic (most exempt vehicles).
keyFacts: Most goods vehicles over 3.5 t (including any trailer) are in scope of assimilated rules.
Assimilated rules apply to journeys within the UK and between the UK and the EU.
AETR rules: international journeys to, from or through AETR countries, not wholly UK–EU.
Most vehicles exempt from assimilated rules come under GB domestic rules on journeys in GB.

keyFacts.text: Even a short spell of assimilated driving in a day means you MUST follow those rules for the whole day.

keyFacts: A vehicle doesn't have to be laden to be in scope of the assimilated or AETR rules.

items.title: Assimilated rules
items.text: Most goods vehicles over 3.5 t, on UK journeys and UK–EU journeys. A tachograph is needed.

items.title: AETR rules
items.text: Journeys to, from or through AETR countries that are not wholly UK–EU, e.g. UK to Norway.

items.title: GB domestic rules
items.text: Most vehicles that are exempt from assimilated rules, while driving in Great Britain.

items.title: Exemptions
items.text: e.g. vehicles that can't exceed 40 km/h, or up to 7.5 t for non-commercial carriage.

a.label: Exemption
points: Applies on UK journeys and on UK–EU journeys
e.g. vehicles not capable of exceeding 40 km/h

b.label: National derogation
points: Applies only to journeys wholly within the UK
e.g. some farming vehicles within 100 km of their base

onTheTest.question: You drive a 12-tonne lorry delivering goods from London to Paris. Which drivers' hours rules apply?
onTheTest.why: Assimilated rules apply to most goods vehicles over 3.5 tonnes used within the UK or on journeys between the UK and the EU.

onTheTest.question: You are driving a lorry from the UK to Norway. Which drivers' hours rules apply?
options: No rules apply outside the EU
onTheTest.why: GV262: journeys between the UK and Liechtenstein or Norway must follow AETR rules.

traps: An empty lorry is still in scope: it does not need to be carrying goods.
UK to Norway or Iceland isn't a UK–EU journey: AETR rules apply.
National derogations only work in the UK. Abroad, only true exemptions apply.
